findings.title: Denial cache pins false denies for 30s after access is granted
findings.body: Check returns Allowed=false as soon as permDenialCache contains the user/action/name/folder key, before consulting either the permission cache or the database. On any deny it then stores that key for shortCacheTTL (30s) and never deletes it when a later load would allow the resource. A check that races ahead of the permission insert for a dashboard or folder the user just created (or any grant after a deny) therefore keeps failing until the denial entry expires, which is the failure this PR is meant to fix. The same pin also freezes denies caused by a stale folder tree in checkInheritedPermissions: once recorded, the denial is served even after folderCache has been rebuilt and inherited access would succeed.

findings.title: Warm permission cache is not trusted for denies, so each new resource hits the DB
findings.body: If cached scopes are present but do not allow the requested resource, Check always falls through to getIdentityPermissions. That path no longer returns the cached set; it singleflight-loads permissions, teams, and the basic role from the DB and overwrites permCache. A just-refreshed cache is therefore ignored for every distinct unauthorized name. The denial cache only dedupes repeats of the same name and folder, and singleflight only coalesces overlapping calls for the same user and action, so sequential Checks (or Checks that do not overlap) each issue a full permission reload. Previously one cached permission set served all checks for that action until TTL.

findings.title: Denial-cache test does not actually grant the cached permission
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck's "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" comment says the permission cache allows dash1 so the test proves the denial entry is what short-circuits. The map value stored is false, so scopeMap["dashboards:uid:dash1"] is not a grant. If the denial-cache read were removed, Check would still deny via the empty fake permission store. The test would pass without the new short-circuit, and nothing covers the creator retry: deny, permission appears in the store, next Check within 30s must be allowed.
